No +EV trade: selling Connecticut, NC, Ventnor, States, or Mediterranean either completes or one-lands a stronger set for them. Cash $473 stays liquid for face denial — Tennessee $180 (block p1 orange; don't outbid), B&O/Short Line $200, Marvin $280, Pacific $300, Boardwalk $400. No mortgage."}}
message.reasoning:
I am playing Monopoly as player p4.

I am reviewing my holdings and opponent positions to plan a legal move.

Opponent p1 owns the orange group but lacks Tennessee, leaving it unowned. p2 owns the green group but lacks North Carolina and Pacific, also unowned. p3 owns the brown group but lacks Mediterranean. These gaps are the main strategic threats.

p3 owns the yellow and dark blue groups but lacks Ventnor and Boardwalk. The bank still holds several unowned properties including Tennessee, B&O, Marvin, Pacific, Short Line, and Boardwalk. My previous trade offer to p3 was rejected. I am now deciding between trading, mortgaging, or ending my turn.

I am weighing a trade with p2. He has cash and the green group, while I block his North Carolina. I will not sell my core holdings to p1 for Connecticut.

Trading for North Carolina would not create a monopoly. Acquiring St. Charles from p2 would leave the pink group incomplete. A two-trade swap for a pink monopoly is too risky and would sacrifice my blockers. I am now considering whether to trade Ventnor for Atlantic or attempt to buy the unowned Marvin.

Acquiring Atlantic from p3 would still require the unowned Marvin. I am now reconsidering a trade with p2, who has cash and the green group.

I have ruled out all remaining trade options. Acquiring more railroads would not improve my rent significantly, and a utility monopoly is too weak to justify giving up a blocker. I will end my turn.

I will not mortgage any properties. I will keep my cash liquid to block p1 from landing on Tennessee. I will keep my blockers in place. I will end my turn.

I am now reconsidering a trade with p3. I would offer Mediterranean for Atlantic plus cash. This would give me two of three yellow properties and leave them with a brown monopoly. I could then buy the unowned Marvin for $280 to complete a yellow monopoly. I have enough cash to cover this.

The trade with p3 is unlikely to succeed. They recently rejected a similar offer for Ventnor plus cash, and they value Atlantic as part of their yellow path. I would still need to buy the unowned Marvin afterward, leaving only $93 to build on my incomplete yellow set. I will not pursue this trade.

I am now reconsidering the trade with p3. Blocking their yellow group would prevent them from completing it, while keeping two of three yellow properties gives me strong denial plus optionality. I am weighing whether a brown monopoly is actually dangerous, since four houses on both properties would cost $400 and leave them with $426.

A $160 hit from four houses on Baltic is survivable with my cash. I will not enable monopolies, and brown is the least dangerous group. Keeping two of three yellow properties still blocks p3 from completing their set.

The trade with p3 is speculative and negative expected value. I will not pursue it. I am now considering a trade with p2 for North Carolina, but that would still leave them needing Pacific to complete their green group.

Selling North Carolina to p2 would leave them one landing away from completing the green group, since Pacific is still unowned. That is too risky. I cannot trade for a completed monopoly from either opponent. Selling Connecticut to p1 would give them an instant light blue monopoly with hotels, which would be devastating.
